page: Amazon Web Services c6a.32xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 3rd generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors running on x86_64 architecture, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs clocked at up to 3.6 GHz with dedicated hardware allocation. The instance features a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, bundling 256.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, or 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core complex.

The instance delivers top-tier parallel compute throughput across synthetic and real-world multi-threaded benchmarks. Stress-ng multi-core tests reached 190,692.91, paired with top-decile results in PassMark CPU tests (98,563.74), Clang software compilation (58,030.0), and synthetic ray tracing (113,760.0). High aggregate memory bandwidth facilitates data ingestion, registering 250.03 GB/sec on uncached read operations. In transactional tests, the platform recorded 137.19 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads alongside 55.53 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs center around instruction set coverage, storage, and acceleration. The EPYC 7R13 microarchitecture supports standard AVX and cryptographic instructions like AES and SHA-NI, but it does not support AVX-512 or AMX matrix extensions. Furthermore, the instance includes no local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating external Amazon EBS volumes for persistence and limiting performance on large neural network inference models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6a.32xlarge offers high compute core density per resource unit relative to memory-heavy alternatives. The system is suited for heavily multi-threaded workloads, including software build farms, batch processing pipelines, video encoding, distributed compute nodes, web application serving tiers, and memory-contained data transformation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro System, featuring AMD EPYC 7R13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 128 dedicated vCPUs (64 physical cores) at 3.6 GHz paired with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Networking throughput is rated at a 50 Gbps baseline. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, requiring external storage for persistent state. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in elevated PassMark CPU, Clang compilation, and Redis throughput results. Without AVX-512 instruction extensions, performance is constrained on advanced vector or large language model workloads compared to standard integer and scalar operations. Delivering high core density relative to memory allocation, c6a.32xlarge is suitable for parallel batch compute, CI/CD compilation farms, distributed web architectures, and high-concurrency microservices.
